title: all-hands-draft-optimize-beta-announcement.json
content:
Purpose: quick draft for All-Hands (Mar 8) announcing Redwood Optimize beta and related Dedicated improvements. This is a working scratchpad — not polished.

Top-line announcement (short):
- Today we’re opening the beta for Redwood Optimize, our toolkit that helps teams reduce inference unit costs while preserving latency and quality.
- Beta includes automatic batching recommendations, workload-aware quantization presets, and integration with the Console’s cost dashboards.
- We’re also shipping latency and autoscale improvements for Dedicated capacity (v1.2) that reduce tail latency for multi-tenant workloads.

Why this matters (1–2 lines for exec):
- Developers get measurable cost wins without rewriting infra or trading off reliability.
- Platform teams get clearer levers to hit unit-economics targets across workloads.

Suggested opening (CEO / Head of Product):
- Quick thank you to the eng + PM teams.
- Frame as our next step in making inference economics predictable and easy to act on.
- One sentence demo tease (show dashboard screenshot during talk).

Key messages / talking points:
- What Optimize does: analyzes real request patterns and suggests batching, caching, and quantization profiles. Provides one-click apply for many recommendations.
- Measurable impact: typical customer workloads saw 15–40% cost reduction in early trials (range depending on sequence length and cache hit rate). Call out case study (internal) — SaaS search team pilot: ~28% cost savings.
- Safety guardrails: recommendations are backed by eval hooks; we run regression tests on chosen prompt sets before applying. Rollback is immediate.
- Beta posture: early access, opt-in, limited capacity. We’ll onboard via Solutions Eng + a small pilot cohort.
- Dedicated v1.2: autoscale improvements, improved batching at the runtime layer, and better KV cache sharing options for low-latency workloads. This is backward compatible — config opt-ins only.

Demo plan (30–60s):
- Show Console: recommendation list -> preview impact -> apply -> show cost preview + dashboard.
- Show before/after latency/cost graphs from internal pilot.

Anticipated questions & suggested answers (Q&A):
Q: How do you measure the cost savings?
A: We simulate your current request mix against suggested profiles and estimate token-level impact + infra-level throughput improvements. We provide both model-level and route-level estimates before you apply anything. (Technical follow-up: we use sampled recent traffic windows; sample sizes adjusted by variance).

Q: Will Optimize change model outputs / affect quality?
A: By default, recommendations prioritize changes that don’t materially affect output quality (e.g., batching, cache). For quantization suggestions we run prompt-set evals and flag any regressions. You get a quality delta report and can rollback instantly.

Q: Is this safe for production?
A: Beta is opt-in. For production rollout we require a staged canary + evaluation gate. We strongly recommend starting with non-critical routes or less-sensitive traffic.

Q: Does this work for Private (VPC/on-prem)?
A: Yes. The same recommendation engine can run on Private control plane (customer-managed), with telemetry kept local per our private deployment design. For air-gapped installs we provide an appliance-style runner (details in Confluence).

Q: How does this affect pricing / contracts?
A: No immediate pricing changes. Optimize is an add-on beta feature. For Dedicated customers we’ll offer professional onboarding + measured uplift guidance before any pricing adjustments.

Internal notes / things to confirm before final announcement:
- Finalize pilot metrics slide (Marcus): need exact % savings, sample size, confidence intervals.
- Legal review for wording around "cost savings" claims (Aisha) — get sign-off by Mar 5.
- Support playbook (Priya): triage steps if a customer reports regression after applying a profile; include rollback steps and logs to collect.
- Console screenshot: ensure no PII and use anonymized tenant. Ops to scrub.
- Beta rollout capacity plan: limit to N=10 pilot customers initially. Who picks the first cohort? (Solutions Eng + Sales suggest list).

Notes to self / working questions:
- Should we mention potential partnerships with HW vendors for quantization optimizations? Maybe later. For all-hands keep it simple.
- Talking point: "we moved the needle on economics" — need a single crisp metric. If pilot numbers are noisy, default to conservative phrasing.
- Be ready for the "why now" question: point to model proliferation + customer ask for cost controls + maturity of our runtime to safely apply these changes.

Callouts for specific people:
- Marcus Lee: final pilot slide + sample artifacts by Mar 4.
- Aisha Patel: legal language + publicity blurb by Mar 5.
- Priya Nair: Support playbook draft and escalation flow by Mar 6.
- Eng infra: confirm Dedicated v1.2 release window & per-route opt-in flag (is flag name optimize_autoscale_v1? confirm).

Next steps (post All-Hands):
- Open sign-ups for beta via a form (link in Confluence) -> Solutions Eng will triage -> onboard first cohort.
- Publish a "How Optimize works" doc in Confluence with technical appendix and evaluation methodology.
- Schedule a cross-functional dry run of the demo (Mar 6) — speaker: Jordan; backup: Marcus.

Tone guidance (for announcement):
- Positive, pragmatic, developer-first. Avoid hyperbole (no "magic"). Highlight measurable wins and safety guardrails.

Rough 2-paragraph announcement copy (for email / Slack):
- "Today we’re opening the beta for Redwood Optimize — a new toolkit that helps teams reduce inference costs while preserving latency and quality. Optimize analyzes your request patterns and recommends batching, caching, and model configuration changes with a one-click apply. Early pilots show meaningful unit-cost improvements; we’ll be running a limited opt-in beta with the Solutions Eng team to onboard pilot customers.
- If you run inference workloads or manage Dedicated capacity, sign up to get early access. We’ll publish a Confluence playbook with technical details, safety checks, and a sign-up form. Expect to see the Optimize card in Console soon where you can preview impact before applying any changes."

Scratch / brainstorming fragments (keep for reference):
- emphasize: "actionable recommendations" not just metrics.
- consider a small customer quote in the final announcement if pilot customer OKs it (ask Legal + CS).
- demo friction points: speed of preview calculation, variability in short-tailed workloads, UI clarity on rollback.

End of draft.

(Again — this is a user-level scratchpad; do not treat as the final canonical announcement. Will iterate with Marcus, Aisha, Priya.)
